body:
Problem:
There is no support for Vim's 'previewpopup' option.

Solution:
Add 'previewpopup' to show :pedit, :ptag, and :psearch previews in a
floating window instead of a split. The value is
"height:N,width:N,border:style"; "border" accepts a named 'winborder'
style and follows 'winborder' when omitted.

Fix #9920

comment_data.body: revert this change.

Not a parallel title mechanism, it fills the float's existing `title/title_chunks`. The preview specific part is only where the value comes from.. it's the previewed file's name, which isn't known when the float is created and changes each time the preview switches files.
Folded it into `win_float_update_preview()` anyway, title, size and position all derive from the just loaded content, so they're set together and the config is applied once instead of twice.

Removed. It was a port of Vim's `update_popups()`, which exists because Vim's popups autosize on every content change, ours only loads once, at `:pedit/:pbuffer` time, so we know the position right there. `win_float_update_preview()` now runs from `do_ecmd()/enter_buffer()`, well before `win_ui_flush()`, so the float is positioned on the first redraw instead of a frame late like the hook was. then removed `w_float_last_changedtick` with it.
I think this could be done together with `prepare_tagpreview` in a followup. Or should we implement it in this PR?

`w_maxwidth/w_maxheight` could be recomputed here, but `w_wantline/w_wantcol` can't, they're the cursor position at creation time `curwin->w_winrow + curwin->w_wrow`, and `win_float_update_preview` runs after focus goes back to the original window (preview is `focusable=false`), so that position is already gone. I’ve added an extensible generic function for parsing comma-separated list options.

```
The option is a comma-separated list of values:
	border		border style (see 'pumborder')
	borderhighlight	highlight group for the popup border characters
	close		show close button: "on" (default) or "off", and if

	height		maximum height of the popup
```
